key_insight: AI coding agents often produce bloated, verbose code not because the final solution needs it, but because the agent’s search process leaves behind speculative edits and abandoned attempts. TRIM shows that reducing the trajectory of the agent’s reasoning/editing path can reduce this "codeSlop."
problem_solved: This paper addresses the problem of AI-generated code being unnecessarily long, messy, and overcomplicated compared with human-written implementations, especially after iterative agentic coding.
method: Analyze the agent’s edit/search trajectory to identify where unnecessary code accumulation happens.
Minimize or prune speculative intermediate steps so only the most useful path to a correct solution remains.
Evaluate how trajectory minimization affects code verbosity and output quality in coding-agent workflows.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that better coding-agent outputs may come from improving the search process, not just the final model. It can lead to cleaner, shorter, more maintainable generated code without sacrificing correctness.
visual_elements: Before-and-after flow diagram showing a long agent trajectory versus a minimized trajectory
Side-by-side code snippet comparison: verbose agent output vs. trimmed output
Pipeline graphic of coding agent steps with abandoned branches highlighted and removed
Bar chart comparing code length / verbosity and pass rate before vs. after TRIM
paper_title: TRIM: Reducing AI-Generated CodeSlop via Agent Trajectory Minimization
paper_authors: Alex Mathai, Shobini Iyer, Aleksandr Nogikh, Petros Maniatis, Franjo Ivancic
